title: Java
tagline: Java from the ground up, the way university courses teach it
description: What a first and second computer-science course in Java cover, in modern Java 25: types, control flow and methods, arrays and ArrayList, recursion, classes, inheritance and interfaces, records, enums and sealed types, generics and the collections framework, exceptions and files, algorithm analysis, searching and sorting, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables and binary search trees built from scratch, lambdas and streams, and threads. Practice compiles and runs in your browser.

milestones.title: First Steps
milestones.blurb: The JDK and your first program, variables and primitive types, operators, strings and input, and control flow.

lessons.title: Java and the JDK: Your First Program
lessons.summary: What Java is and how it runs - source code, the compiler, bytecode and the JVM - installing the JDK, the shape of a Java program with a class and a main method, printing with System.out, comments, compiling and running from the command line, and reading compiler errors.

lessons.title: Variables and Primitive Types
lessons.summary: Declaring and assigning variables, the eight primitive types and their ranges, literals, var, constants with final, primitive versus reference types, widening and narrowing conversions with casts, integer overflow, and naming conventions.

lessons.title: Operators and Math
lessons.summary: Arithmetic with integer division and remainder, compound assignment and increment, comparison and logical operators with short-circuiting, the ternary operator, precedence, the Math class, and comparing doubles safely.

lessons.title: Strings and Input
lessons.summary: Working with String - its common methods, immutability, comparing with equals instead of ==, escapes and text blocks, formatting with printf and String.format - and reading keyboard input with Scanner, including the nextInt/nextLine trap.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.summary: Making decisions with if and else, the classic switch statement and the modern switch expression with arrows, loops with while, do-while, for and the enhanced for, break and continue, labelled breaks for nested loops, and input loops with a sentinel.

milestones.title: Methods, Arrays and Recursion
milestones.blurb: Methods, arrays, ArrayList and wrapper types, recursion, and strings in depth.

lessons.title: Methods
lessons.summary: Defining static methods with parameters and return types, void methods, calling methods, pass-by-value for primitives and references, overloading, variable-length arguments, local variables and scope, returning early, and designing small methods that do one thing.

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.summary: Creating arrays with new and initializers, indexing and length, default values, looping over arrays, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, the java.util.Arrays helpers (toString, sort, fill, copyOf, equals, binarySearch), copying versus sharing, two-dimensional arrays, and classic array algorithms.

lessons.title: ArrayList and Wrapper Types
lessons.summary: The growable ArrayList - adding, getting, setting, removing, searching and sorting - the List interface, wrapper classes like Integer and Double, autoboxing and its traps (remove by index or value, == on Integers, null unboxing), List.of, and iterating while removing safely.

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.summary: Methods that call themselves - base cases and recursive cases, how the call stack works, tracing factorial and Fibonacci, recursion on arrays and strings, the cost of naive recursion and memoization, StackOverflowError, and when to prefer a loop.

lessons.title: Strings in Depth
lessons.summary: Characters as numbers and the Character class, walking through strings, why repeated concatenation is slow and how StringBuilder fixes it, string comparison and sorting, splitting with regular expressions, a first look at Pattern and Matcher, and converting between strings, chars and numbers.

milestones.title: Object-Oriented Programming
milestones.blurb: Classes and objects, encapsulation and static members, inheritance and polymorphism, interfaces and abstract classes, records, enums and sealed types.

lessons.title: Classes and Objects
lessons.summary: Defining your own classes with fields, constructors and instance methods, creating objects with new, the this reference, references and null, toString, object identity versus equality, and how to design a class around the data it owns.

lessons.title: Encapsulation, Constructors and static
lessons.summary: Access modifiers and why fields should be private, getters and setters with validation, constructor overloading and this(...), immutable classes with final fields, static fields and methods, static factory methods, constants, and when a class should be a utility class.

lessons.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
lessons.summary: Extending a class with extends, calling the superclass constructor with super, overriding methods and @Override, protected members, dynamic dispatch and polymorphism, the Object class with toString, equals and hashCode, casting with instanceof patterns, final, and when to prefer composition.

lessons.title: Interfaces and Abstract Classes
lessons.summary: Abstract classes and abstract methods, interfaces as contracts, implementing several interfaces, default and static interface methods, programming to an interface, the built-in Comparable and Iterable, functional interfaces as a preview of lambdas, and choosing between an interface and an abstract class.

lessons.title: Records, Enums and Sealed Types
lessons.summary: Modern Java data modelling - records with compact constructors and value equality, enums with fields, methods and switch, EnumMap, sealed interfaces that list their implementations, and pattern matching in switch with record patterns for exhaustive handling of every case.

milestones.title: Generics, Collections and Exceptions
milestones.blurb: Generics, the collections framework, Comparable and Comparator, exceptions, and files with java.nio.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.summary: Type parameters on classes, interfaces and methods, why generics replaced Object and casts, bounded types with extends, wildcards with ? extends and ? super (PECS), type erasure and its limits, and writing your own generic container.

lessons.title: The Collections Framework
lessons.summary: The interfaces and implementations of java.util - List, Set, Map, Queue and Deque with ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, HashMap, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap, ArrayDeque and PriorityQueue - choosing between them, iterating, counting and grouping with maps, the equals and hashCode contract, and immutable collections.

lessons.title: Comparable, Comparator and Sorting
lessons.summary: Natural ordering with Comparable, external orderings with Comparator, building comparators with comparing, thenComparing, reversed and nullsFirst, sorting lists and arrays, stability, sorted collections with custom orderings, the compareTo contract, and common mistakes like subtracting to compare.

lessons.title: Exceptions
lessons.summary: Throwing and catching exceptions, the exception hierarchy, checked versus unchecked exceptions and the throws clause, multi-catch, finally, try-with-resources, custom exception classes with causes, stack traces, and good practice for validating arguments and handling errors.

lessons.title: Files and I/O
lessons.summary: Reading and writing text files with java.nio.file - Path and Files, readString, readAllLines, lines and write, BufferedReader and BufferedWriter for large files, character encodings, directories and walking them, handling IOException, parsing CSV records, and the older java.io classes you will still meet.

milestones.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
milestones.blurb: Big O, searching and sorting, and linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables and binary search trees built from scratch.

lessons.title: Algorithm Analysis and Big O
lessons.summary: How to compare algorithms independently of computers - counting basic steps, Big O notation and the common growth classes from O(1) to O(2^n), analysing loops, nested loops and halving, best, worst and average cases, the costs of Java's collection operations, measuring with System.nanoTime, and space complexity.

lessons.title: Searching and Sorting
lessons.summary: Linear and binary search with their invariants and the overflow-safe midpoint, the simple sorts (selection and insertion) and why they are O(n²), divide and conquer with merge sort and quicksort, stability, choosing a pivot, and what Java's own sorts use.

lessons.title: Linked Lists
lessons.summary: Building a singly linked list from nodes - adding at the front and back with a tail reference, getting by index, removing, reversing in place, iterating with Iterator, the edge cases of empty and one-element lists, doubly linked lists and sentinel nodes, and comparing linked lists with array lists.

lessons.title: Stacks, Queues and Hash Tables
lessons.summary: Implementing a growable array list with amortised O(1) appends, a stack and its uses (undo, bracket matching, expression evaluation), a circular-buffer queue, and a hash table with chaining - hash functions, buckets, load factor and resizing - and why equals and hashCode matter.

tasks.title: A min-stack and a hash set

lessons.title: Trees and Binary Search Trees
lessons.summary: Trees and their vocabulary, binary trees, the binary search tree property, recursive insert, search and delete including the two-child case, in-order, pre-order, post-order and level-order traversal, height and balance, why balanced trees like Java's TreeMap guarantee O(log n), and heaps for priority queues.

milestones.title: Streams, Threads and Projects
milestones.blurb: Lambdas and functional interfaces, the Stream API, modern Java features, threads and concurrency, and a complete program with packages and tests.

lessons.title: Lambdas and Functional Interfaces
lessons.summary: Passing behaviour as a value - functional interfaces, lambda syntax, method references, the java.util.function interfaces (Function, Predicate, Consumer, Supplier, BiFunction, UnaryOperator), composing functions, effectively final captured variables, and lambdas with the collections API (forEach, removeIf, replaceAll, sort, computeIfAbsent).

lessons.title: The Stream API
lessons.summary: Processing data declaratively with streams - creating streams, intermediate operations (filter, map, flatMap, sorted, distinct, limit), terminal operations (collect, toList, count, reduce, anyMatch, min, max), primitive streams and summary statistics, Collectors for grouping, partitioning, joining and mapping, laziness, and when a loop is clearer.

lessons.title: Optional and Modern Java
lessons.summary: Representing maybe-missing values with Optional and its methods (map, filter, orElse, orElseGet, orElseThrow, ifPresent), when not to use it, and a tour of modern Java features - var, text blocks, switch expressions and pattern matching, records and sealed types together, the java.time date API, and immutable collections.

lessons.title: Threads and Concurrency
lessons.summary: Running work at the same time - threads and Runnable, joining, race conditions and why count++ is unsafe, synchronized and locks, atomic variables and concurrent collections, ExecutorService and Future, CompletableFuture, virtual threads, deadlock, and the rule of sharing as little mutable state as possible.

lessons.title: Project: A Complete Program
lessons.summary: How a real Java program is organised - packages and the folder layout, access across packages, Maven and Gradle with a pom.xml or build.gradle, dependencies, unit tests with JUnit 5, building a runnable JAR, and the plan for the final project, a command-driven event planner.
